metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model tends to overestimate early in the horizon and underestimates sharp drops; apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days after spikes.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day averages in early cycles; reduce forecast by 2–5% for first 10 days of horizon.
- After a spike (e.g., >45.0), model overshoots by 3–8% in next 3–7 days; apply decayed smoothing to prevent overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop >10% from prior day, model often fails to adjust; add 1–3 day lagged correction to prevent premature recovery.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day windows; if forecast is >1.5σ above mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0σ per day until convergence.
- Sentiment history is all 0.00 → no behavioral signal → model should not assume sentiment-driven volatility; treat as pure technical correction.
